palette.noAi: The assistant is not in Admin yet. Search and navigation work without it.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Use the account you created on this server.
login.totpHint: Open your authenticator app and type the 6-digit code.
login.totpAuto: You can paste the whole code. It sends by itself when all 6 digits are in.
login.locked: Temporarily locked after too many attempts. Wait and try again.
login.pwChanged: Password changed and signed out everywhere. Sign in with your new password.

setup.title: Set up your server
setup.intro: Create the admin account. The dashboard is next.
setup.certTitle: Why your browser showed a warning.
setup.certBody: You opened this server by its IP address, so it uses a certificate it made for itself. The connection is still encrypted. The warning goes away once the server has a domain.
setup.promise: No domain questions · No cloud account · Your data stays on this server

apps.title: Apps
apps.nAttention: {n} need attention | {n} needs attention | {n} need attention
apps.emptyTitle: Your server is ready. Install your first app.
apps.emptyBody: Pick an app and it starts by itself, with a domain and a certificate set up for you.
apps.pairHint: Want a free web address like shop.yourteam.keenrig.com?
apps.pairUndo: optional, your apps run without it
apps.applyingHint: Can take a few minutes the first time. This page updates by itself.
apps.attentionNext: Open it to see what you can do.
apps.removing: {app} is being removed. It disappears from this server in a moment.

store.title: App Store
store.subtitle: Apps start on install — domain and certificate are set up once the server has a name.
store.empty: No apps are packaged on this server yet. Ask for the app you need on Keenrig Console.
store.name: Name
store.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Leave empty to use the app's default.
store.domainPh: Leave empty if you have none yet
store.domainHint: Follows the name until you edit it by hand. The certificate is set up for you.
store.memoryFreeNotReported: Free memory on this server: not reported
store.conflict: That name or domain is already used by another app. Choose another name.
store.errLicenseLimit: This server has reached the app limit of its plan. Remove an app, or upgrade on Keenrig Console, then try again — the name is not the problem.
store.errQuota: This server does not have enough capacity left for another app. Stop an app you don't use, or free some memory or disk, then try again.
store.requestTitle: Don't see the app you need?
store.requestBody: Tell us on Keenrig Console. Other people can vote for it there.
store.noMatchBody: Ask for it on Keenrig Console. Requests with more votes are packaged first.

detail.syncApplying: Applying your latest changes… The current version keeps running meanwhile.
detail.stepApplying: Starting the app with these settings
detail.rolloutHint: The current version keeps serving until the new one is healthy.
detail.savesAs: {app} keeps running on its current settings until the new ones are healthy.
detail.noChanges: No changes yet — edit a field to see exactly what will change before you apply.
detail.applied: Saved — the server applies it within a few seconds.
detail.guardTitle: You have {n} unsaved change in Configuration. | You have {n} unsaved changes in Configuration.
detail.noDomains: This app has no domains yet.
detail.domainSuggested: Suggested: {fqdn} — add it below to serve the app at this address with HTTPS.
detail.domainHint: First, where you bought the domain, point its A record at this server’s IP address. HTTPS starts working once the name reaches this server.
detail.domainTaken: That domain is already attached to another app.
detail.removeDomainWarn: Remove {fqdn}? The app stops answering at this address right away and its certificate is dropped.
detail.deleteWarn: Uninstall {slug}? The app and all of its data are deleted from this server. This cannot be undone.
detail.logsTitle: Logs are not in Admin yet.
detail.logsBody: Run this on the server to see the last 200 lines of this app:
detail.bkTitle: Backups run from the terminal for now.
detail.bkBody: Find the backup you want, then restore only this app. Other apps and server settings are not touched.
detail.bkHint: Replace <id> with a backup ID from the list. Run as root.
detail.syncFirst: Starting for the first time — the server is downloading the app. This can take a few minutes.
detail.rolloutFirst: The server downloads the app first, which can take a few minutes. This page updates by itself.
detail.imageHint: Which build of the app runs. Change it only if the app’s maker or Keenrig support tells you to.
detail.attnNext: Check its logs for the reason. If this started after you changed Configuration, change it back. If it keeps failing, back up its data, then uninstall it and install it again from the App Store.
detail.deleteType: Type the app name to confirm:

domains.title: Domains
domains.sub: Every web address your apps use. HTTPS certificates are set up automatically.
domains.addTitle: Add a domain to an app
domains.name: Domain
domains.cloudReadOnly: Keenrig Cloud gave this server its name; it is managed in the Console and cannot be edited here.
domains.localHint: This name was set when Keenrig was installed on this server. To change it, ask whoever manages the server (it is the KEENRIG_DOMAIN setting of the keenrig service).
domains.emptyBody: Every domain belongs to an app — install an app first, then add names to it.
domains.ownBody: Add an A record for the name where you bought it, pointing at this server's public IP address. Keep any other records you already have. The certificate is issued once the name resolves here.
domains.digLabel: Check where a name points — works in Command Prompt, PowerShell or Terminal
domains.digHint: Under “Address” it should show this server’s public IP address. DNS changes can take up to an hour.

events.title: Activity
events.sub: What happened on this server, newest first.
events.emptyBody: Installs, sign-ins and changes show up here.

cloud.notPairedSub: Optional link to Keenrig Console. This server runs on its own right now.
cloud.staleKeep: Your apps keep running. Nothing on this server depends on the connection.
cloud.stillWorksList: Apps, Admin, sign-in, backups to your own storage
cloud.pausedList: Console sync, cloud AI, new certificates for the Keenrig name
cloud.ownTitle: This server runs on its own.
cloud.what2: Manage this server from Keenrig Console
cloud.keep3: Admin and sign-in on this server
cloud.undoHint: Connecting is optional — apps and data stay on this server either way.
cloud.linkedTo: Linked to {cloud} as environment {env} · last check-in {ago}
cloud.pfTitle: If this server is disconnected from Keenrig Cloud
cloud.pfStopName: Keenrig name {name} and its certificate renewal
cloud.pfAtRisk: {apps} would stop being reachable at their keenrig.com addresses.
cloud.pfDataKept: Their data is kept. Add your own domain to each one first.
cloud.pfNotInUiTitle: Disconnecting is not in Admin yet.
cloud.pfNotInUiBody: This list is here so nothing surprises you when it is. You can connect again later with a new join token.
cloud.stateUnavailable: Connection state not reported — this server does not report it yet.
cloud.step1: Open Keenrig Console → Add environment → at the server step pick “I have my own machine”.
cloud.step2: The Console shows a join token — copy it and paste it here:
cloud.tokenBad: That is not a join token — it is 64 characters of 0-9 a-f; copy it whole from the Console.
cloud.waitingSync: The Console accepted this server (environment {env}). Waiting for its first check-in…
cloud.syncSlow: No check-in after 60 seconds. Check on the server:
cloud.altTitle: Or run a command on the server
cloud.altBody: The Console also shows an install command with the token. Run it on this server over SSH — on an installed server it only connects; nothing is reinstalled, apps and data stay:

backup.title: Backups
backup.sub: Backups run from the terminal on this server for now.
backup.noScheduleTitle: Nothing runs on a schedule yet.
backup.noScheduleBody: Run a backup yourself before big changes. A Backups page with a schedule is coming; until then, these commands do the real work.
backup.rootHint: Run these as root (sudo -i). They read the backup storage and passphrase from
backup.cmdRestoreAppNote: on this server — use the app ID, not its name
backup.passWarn: Without your passphrase, backups cannot be restored.
backup.passWarnBody: Keenrig never stores KEENRIG_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE. Keep it somewhere other than this server.
backup.encBody: Every backup is encrypted. It contains this server’s keys, so encryption can’t be turned off.
backup.noDefault: There is no default destination: a wrong default would quietly write backups to this server's own disk — lost at the same moment as what it protects.
backup.notYet1: Data in app add-on databases (postgres, redis)
backup.notYet3: Choosing a destination and restoring from Admin
backup.who: These commands run on the server itself, by someone who can log in to it (SSH). If that isn’t you, send this page to whoever set up your server.

settings.sub: This server, this browser, and what Admin can't do yet.
settings.themeHint: Saved in this browser. Auto follows your system setting.
settings.updatesBody: This server updates itself. It checks for a new Keenrig release every 5 minutes, installs it, checks that everything still works, and goes back to the previous version by itself if not. You don’t need to do anything.
settings.aiBody: Not in Admin yet. Search (Ctrl K) works without it.
settings.activityBody: What happened on this server, newest first.
settings.notYetBody: Users and groups, services, system details.
settings.tfaOffHint: Recommended: also ask for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator…) at every sign-in.
settings.tfaOnHint: Every sign-in asks for a 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
settings.tfaOffWarn: Without it, your password alone opens Admin. Enter your password to confirm.
settings.tfaStep1: In your authenticator app, add an account and choose “Enter a setup key”. Type this key:
settings.tfaOpenApp: On this phone? Open it in your authenticator app instead
settings.tfaStep2: Type the 6-digit code the app shows:
settings.tfaOnDone: Two-factor code is on. Your next sign-in will ask for it.
settings.pwHint: After the change you are signed out everywhere, including here. Sign in again with the new password.
settings.peopleNotYet: One admin account for now — adding more people is not in Admin yet.
settings.updatesTechBody: Runs as the systemd timer keenrig-upgrade. Each release is checked against its sha256 checksum; releases are not signed yet. There is no update screen in Admin yet.
